title: Integration along a vector bundle
statement:
Let $N\geq1$ be an integer, $A$ a finite commutative ring with $NA=0$, and $S$ a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible. Let $\pi:E\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant rank $d\geq0$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Work in the ordinary derived category $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of constant-coefficient module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Use the ordinary etale Tate sheaves $A_T(1)=\mu_{N,T}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A_T$, their tensor powers $A_T(d)$ and their canonical pullback identifications [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The relative-spectrum construction makes $\pi$ affine [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], hence quasi-compact and separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Around every point of $E$, choose an affine trivializing open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $S$; its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}R[x_1,\ldots,x_d]$, a finitely generated $R$-algebra. Thus $\pi$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-pointwise-criterion], and quasi-compactness makes it finite type. Consequently $E$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The base $S$ is quasi-compact by its Noetherian hypothesis and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], so [thm-nagata-compactification] supplies a compactification of $\pi$. Use $R\pi_!$ of [def-amb-etale-compact-support], with its compactification-independent interpretation on bounded-below inputs [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons], and put
$$C_\pi=R\pi_!\bigl(A_E(d)[2d]\bigr),\qquad L_\pi=\mathcal H^0(C_\pi).$$
Here cohomology sheaves and shifts have the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

The integration map
$$t_\pi:C_\pi\longrightarrow A_S[0]$$
is defined by the following construction. Choose a Zariski open cover $u_i:U_i\hookrightarrow S$ and linear trivializations $E\times_SU_i\cong\mathbf A^d_{U_i}$ from [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Restrict compact support using the exchange isomorphism of [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], and use the Tate pullback identifications. In the chosen coordinates compose with the specified affine-space trace of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], obtaining
$$a_i:u_i^*C_\pi\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_{d,U_i!}A_{\mathbf A^d_{U_i}}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{t_{p_{d,U_i}}}A_{U_i}[0].$$
Writing $\phi_i:E|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf A^d_{U_i}$ for the chosen coordinates, this identification is the exchange map for the square over $1_{U_i}$ with top map $\phi_i^{-1}:\mathbf A^d_{U_i}\to E|_{U_i}$, followed by the canonical coefficient identification. The square is Cartesian because $\phi_i^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. Every $U_i$ and overlap $U_i\cap U_j$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. The compactification and its base changes are therefore between Noetherian schemes. The input sheaf shifted by $2d$ has cohomology vanishing outside degree $-2d$, so it is bounded below and both the compact-support comparison and the exchange theorem apply. The affine-space trace is an isomorphism. Exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] identifies the restrictions of $\mathcal H^q(C_\pi)$ with $\mathcal H^q(u_i^*C_\pi)$. Thus $\mathcal H^q(C_\pi)=0$ for $q\ne0$: each restricts to zero on the cover, and the underlying abelian sheaf is zero by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-detects-iso], applied to its map to zero.

Take $\lambda_i=\mathcal H^0(a_i):L_\pi|_{U_i}\to A_{U_i}$. On $W=U_i\cap U_j$ the two coordinate systems differ by a matrix in $\operatorname{GL}_d(\mathcal O_S(W))$ [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Write $B_i$ and $B_j$ for the coordinate identifications from $(C_\pi)|_W$ to $Rp_{d,W!}A_{\mathbf A^d_W}(d)[2d]$. Put $K_W=A_{\mathbf A^d_W}(d)[2d]$. For $g\in\operatorname{GL}_d(\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W))$, write $a_g(v)=gv$ and use precisely the pullback action of [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance]:
$$\rho_g=Rp_{d,W!}(\theta_g)\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{!,a_g}:Rp_{d,W!}K_W\longrightarrow Rp_{d,W!}K_W,\qquad\theta_g:a_g^*K_W\xrightarrow{\sim}K_W.$$
Here exchange is for the Cartesian square whose two vertical maps are $p_{d,W}$, whose bottom map is $1_W$ and whose top map is $a_g$; $\theta_g$ is the canonical Tate pullback identification. Restrict $\phi_i$ and $\phi_j$ to $E|_W$ and define $g$ by $a_g=\phi_i\circ\phi_j^{-1}$. This is an invertible linear substitution by [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]; if the frames in that definition satisfy $e^{(j)}_k=\sum_lG_{lk}e^{(i)}_l$, then $\phi_j=a_{G^{\mathsf T}}\circ\phi_i$ and $g=(G^{\mathsf T})^{-1}$. In particular $\phi_j^{-1}=\phi_i^{-1}\circ a_g$. Paste the two Cartesian squares over $1_W$ whose top maps are $\phi_i^{-1}$ and $a_g$. Their composite is the square with top map $\phi_j^{-1}$. Horizontal pasting in [thm-cbc-finite-torsion] identifies its exchange with the composite of these two exchanges; composition compatibility of the Tate identifications then gives $B_j=\rho_g\circ B_i$. The restriction formula in [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] and the same pasting give $a_i|_W=t_{p_{d,W}}\circ B_i$ and $a_j|_W=t_{p_{d,W}}\circ B_j$. The scheme $W$ is Noetherian, $N$ remains invertible on $W$, the coefficient ring is the same finite ring $A$ with $NA=0$, and $g$ is an invertible matrix of global functions on $W$. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance] hold over $W$, and its actual equality is $t_{p_{d,W}}\circ\rho_g=t_{p_{d,W}}$. Hence
$$a_j|_W=t_{p_{d,W}}\circ\rho_g\circ B_i=t_{p_{d,W}}\circ B_i=a_i|_W.$$
Taking $\mathcal H^0$ gives $\lambda_j|_W=\lambda_i|_W$. Define $\lambda:L_\pi\to A_S$ by the unique gluing of this family in [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing].

For clarity, the identification $\alpha_\pi:C_\pi\xrightarrow{\sim}L_\pi[0]$ used in the definition is the following truncation roof. For a representing complex $K$ of $C_\pi$, let $b:\tau_{\leq0}K\to K$ be the inclusion and $c:\tau_{\leq0}K\to\mathcal H^0(K)[0]$ the projection from cycles to cohomology in degree zero, zero in negative degrees. It is a chain map: in degree $-1$ the equation is $c^0d_K^{-1}=0$ because the quotient $\ker d_K^0\to\ker d_K^0/\operatorname{im}d_K^{-1}$ kills boundaries; in every other degree the chain-map equation has both sides zero. The truncation and its cohomology are as in [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology]; its descended projection is the $j_0$ of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends]. Both $b$ and $c$ induce the identity on degree-zero cohomology, and all other cohomology objects of their sources and targets vanish. Hence both are quasi-isomorphisms, and set $\alpha_\pi=Q(c)\circ Q(b)^{-1}$, where $Q$ is the localization functor [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Finally define
$$t_\pi=\lambda[0]\circ\alpha_\pi.$$
Exact restriction preserves the kernels and quotients defining $b$ and $c$, so it preserves this roof. The degree-zero calculation gives $\mathcal H^0(\alpha_\pi)=1_{L_\pi}$. For a chain map $f:K\to K'$ between degree-zero-cohomology complexes, the inclusions and quotient projections satisfy $f\circ b_K=b_{K'}\circ\tau_{\leq0}f$ and $\mathcal H^0(f)[0]\circ c_K=c_{K'}\circ\tau_{\leq0}f$. Inverting $Q(b_K)$ and $Q(b_{K'})$ therefore gives $\alpha_{K'}\circ Q(f)=\mathcal H^0(f)[0]\circ\alpha_K$. The inclusion $b:\tau_{\leq0}\to\mathrm{id}$ is a natural transformation on all complexes, and $\tau_{\leq0}$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends]. The localization property of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] therefore descends $b$ to a natural transformation on the derived category: its naturality equation holds for every image of a chain map, hence also for the inverse of the image of a quasi-isomorphism and for composites of these generators. The projection $c$ descends naturally by [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-descends]. Applying these two descended naturality equations to any derived morphism between degree-zero-cohomology objects and inverting $b$ at its source and target proves the displayed naturality of $\alpha$ in the derived category. Taking an isomorphism between two representatives of $C_\pi$ proves independence of the representative. On $U_i$, compose $a_i$ with $(\alpha_\pi|_{U_i})^{-1}$: this is a morphism $L_\pi|_{U_i}[0]\to A_{U_i}[0]$ whose $\mathcal H^0$ is $\lambda_i$. Full faithfulness of the degree-zero embedding [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] makes this morphism exactly $\lambda_i[0]$. Thus $t_\pi|_{U_i}=a_i$. For two choices of cover, use the intersections of their opens as a common refinement; the displayed overlap calculation applies to the two frames on each intersection, so the sheaf maps agree there and unique sheaf gluing makes their global maps equal. For any derived morphism with these local restrictions, composition with $\alpha_\pi^{-1}$ corresponds by the same full faithfulness to a sheaf map with restrictions $\lambda_i$; unique sheaf gluing forces it to be $\lambda$. Thus this construction specifies the unique derived morphism restricting to these prescribed affine-space traces. This definition uses ordinary etale twists and ordinary etale compact support; identification with pro-etale coefficient constructions is a separate comparison. At $d=0$ the prescribed local trace is the identity adjunction trace of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace].

proof.text: On a frame cover, identify the compact-support source with the affine trace source. Exact inverse image and cover conservativity give concentration outside degree zero.
Apply the general unique degree-zero normalized identification to obtain alpha:C_pi≅single(H^0(C_pi)).

The local Hom correspondence gives local sheaf maps. The overlap equality makes them a matching family, so the étale family gluing theorem gives lambda. To verify any other frame and any normalized data, enlarge the chosen cover by that frame and use uniqueness on the original cover.

The local Hom correspondence converts the sheaf restriction equations into the original derived normalization. Unique alpha and sheaf gluing prove unique (alpha,lambda), and the unchanged definition is single(lambda) composed with alpha.

lean.note: The actual inverse-frame exchange and canonical Tate comparisons specify every local map. The defining map is alpha.hom followed by singleFunctor.map lambda. Alpha and lambda are selected only from an existence-and-uniqueness theorem: H^0(alpha) is the identity and their composite has the specified trace on every frame. Its proof docstring gives the sheaf gluing and the truncation roof Q(c) Q(b)^(-1); the theorem also states concentration in degree zero. No extra normalized projective-line datum is assumed by the definition. blueprint_update.statement:
Let $\pi:E\to S$ be a vector bundle of constant
rank $d$, in the sense of
[def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Its integration
map

$$
t_\pi:R\pi_!A_E(d)[2d]\longrightarrow A_S
$$

is the map which on a trivializing open set is the
affine-space integration of
[lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace], glued over a trivializing cover.
Here $(d)$ denotes the Tate twist.

proof.text:
These maps glue as morphisms of sheaves: the source has cohomology only in
degree zero on a trivializing cover, and [lem-amb-linear-trace-invariance]
identifies the maps on every overlap.
